newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita's interim parent profit seen rising 15%.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita's interim parent profit seen rising 15%.

text.p: The weaker yen and a strong showing in the information sector at home are expected to help Japanese electronics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd post a healthy rise in half-year profits later this month.

Analysts say a recovery in sales of household appliances such as refrigerators and washing machines will also contribute to an expected rise of around 15 percent in the company's parent profits for the April-September period.

"I see no factors that are detrimental to Matsushita's parent company business, except for higher air-conditioner inventories, which may affect its business next year," said Nikko Research Center analyst Hideki Watanabe.

Matsushita, whose products are sold under the "National", "Panasonic" and "Technics" brand names, will announce parent-only earnings for April to September, the first half of fiscal 1996/97, on October 25.

It will announce group-based results in late November. The fall in the value of the yen against the dollar by more than 10 yen year-on-year will have more of a positive impact on the group-based results.

Nomura Research Institute analyst Kiyotaka Teranishi said he expected Matsushita's parent current profit to rise 14 percent to 48 billion yen ($432 million). Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities such as investments in stocks.
"Continuing price declines in the domestic market will be offset by increased sales volume," Teranishi said.
Nikko predicts a profits rise of about the same size.

A surge in the number of new homes being built in Japan, fuelled by low interest rates and a looming rise in the nation's sales tax, is expected to push up domestic shipments of refrigerators, air conditioners, televisions and washing machines to record highs in calendar 1996.

Matsushita is also expected to benefit from a mobile phone boom in Japan. Nikko's Watanabe estimated that its sales of information-related goods may have risen 14.8 percent in the half year due to the boom, with a 2.7 percent sales rise expected in home appliances.
But he said Matsushita's swollen air conditioner stocks, estimated at 2.5 million units at the end of September, may damage its business next year.

On a group basis, Watanabe estimates Matsushita's net six-month profits will be 44 billion yen ($396 million), a turnaround from a net loss of 132.9 billion yen ($1.19 billion) a year earlier, when it posted a large foreign exchange loss following the sale of U.S. film-making unit MCA Inc.
The weaker yen has dramatically improved the performance of export-dependent units such as Matsushita-Kotobuki Electronics Industries Ltd, which were hit hard by the strong yen a year ago, he said.
Analysts are focusing on whether Matsushita will raise its full-year forecasts to reflect the yen's sharp depreciation.
Matsushita's forecasts are currently based on a rate of 95 yen to the dollar. ($1=111 yen)
